source_title: oxnw/ai-phone: A SIP phone daemon with local speech and language models on Apple Silicon. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
An AI phone agent that runs on your computer.
Documentation · Architecture · AGPL-3.0
The installer adds ai-phone to ~/.local/bin . If it prints a PATH command, run that command in this terminal and add it to your shell’s startup file for future terminals. Then start setup:
To add the command to an existing installation, rerun ./scripts/install.sh from your updated checkout. Keep the checkout and its .venv in place; the command uses them from any directory.
Setup lets you choose incoming calls, outgoing calls, or both, then configures the model, line and voice. It recommends a local model based on detected RAM and downloads the required weights. Use ai-phone setup --plain for plain prompts. For SignalWire, buy a number in its portal first, then connect it in setup; see the SignalWire guide .
The current speech backends use MLX on Apple Silicon, even when a cloud model handles the conversation. Supporting Linux or Windows would require different speech backends and changes to installation and platform integration. The platform requirement applies to the computer running ai-phone; callers can use any phone or SIP client.
Keep it running while you want to receive calls. For outgoing calls only, start it when needed and stop it with Ctrl-C afterward. Setup does not install a background service.
From another terminal, give the phone agent instructions for a call:
Replace the example number with the number you want to call. The command returns the transcript when the call ends. Every outgoing call starts with an AI disclosure. Incoming calls use the greeting and instructions you set during setup. English and one call at a time are currently supported.
For a free local test, enable incoming calls, select A SIP address in setup, and keep the name agent :
Run setup again to change the voice, model, call directions or caller ID, then restart the daemon.
An agent with shell access can use relay mode to control each turn:
With no active call, listen --json waits for an incoming call and handles it in relay mode. Each command with --json returns one JSON object on stdout; call also sends progress events to stderr. An unanswered relay turn times out after 25 seconds by default. See the command reference for call IDs, transcript retrieval, timeouts and exit codes.
Speech recognition and synthesis stay local. A remote language model receives the call's text, instructions and conversation history. An external agent's cloud provider also sees any transcripts passed to it. Phone audio travels over SIP/RTP; carrier charges and subscription limits apply.
Usage guide : lines, forwarding, caller ID, models and CLI reference.
SignalWire guide : existing numbers, SIP credentials, caller ID and TLS.
Example configuration : available settings.
Architecture : components and call flow.
NAT checklist : network configuration.
Measurements : latest local call and interruption results.
Install and setup have been checked from a fresh clone. Local call and interruption tests have run. Basic calls between SignalWire and Telnyx US numbers exchanged speech in both directions; see the verification details and remaining checks . Long-running SignalWire registration and end-to-end agent acceptance checks remain pending.
The latest published local benchmark (27 October 2026) measured 1.50 s median first-audible response under heavy memory pressure; it missed the one-second target. Full conditions and earlier results are documented.
AGPL-3.0-or-later . The bundled PJSIP interface files use GPLv2-or-later ; see the license notes .
